claim.claim: Walmart's results for the quarter ended April 30, 2026 show that its international business is a drag on overall profitability.

verdict.label: CONTRADICTED

contradicting_evidence.quote: Operating income $ 1,602 $ 1,293 Percentage of net sales Gross profit 21.1 % 21.1 % Operating expenses 17.8 % 18.1 % Operating income 4.6 % 4.3 %

verdict.reasoning_summary:
The claim asserts that Walmart's international business is "a drag on overall profitability" for the quarter ended April 30, 2026. This is an interpretive claim about the quality/impact of the international segment on profitability.

Evidence E4 shows that for the three months ended April 30, 2026, Walmart International had:
- Operating income of $1,602 million (up from $1,293 million in the prior year)
- Operating margin of 4.6% (up from 4.3% in the prior year)

The international segment was profitable with an operating margin of 4.6%, and this margin actually improved year-over-year by 30 basis points. A segment that generates positive operating income and improving margins cannot reasonably be characterized as "a drag on overall profitability." While the 4.6% operating margin may be lower than other segments, the segment is still contributing positively to overall profitability rather than dragging it down.

The evidence directly contradicts the claim's characterization of the international business as a drag on profitability.
